name: Learn: CIS Benchmarks (kube-bench, hardened)
objective: CKS › Cluster Setup + System Hardening (10% + 15%). Drill the kube-bench workflow harder than the exam: run it as a Job against node AND master, read [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WARN], then remediate every recurring finding — manifest & PKI file modes, the kubelet read-only port, the apiserver NodeRestriction plugin — plus a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Seven strict, node-level practicals on auditing a real multi-node cluster against the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark with kube-bench and remediating its findings. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Audit a worker node with kube-bench
questions.teach:
**kube-bench** audits a node against the **CIS Kubernetes Benchmark**, printing `[PASS]`, `[FAIL]`, or `[WARN]` per numbered control. Because it inspects the host's real files, run it **on the node** — as a Job with `hostPID: true` and hostPath mounts — and read findings from the pod logs.

**Gotcha:** a plain pod without `hostPID` and host mounts reads the container's filesystem, not the host, giving bogus results.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-bench`, create a Job named `kube-bench` using image `aquasec/kube-bench:latest` with args `["run","--targets","node"]`, `hostPID: true`, `restartPolicy: Never`, and hostPath mounts for `/var/lib/kubelet`, `/etc/kubernetes`, and `/etc/systemd`. Wait for it to complete.

Target: Job `kube-bench` in `cks-bench` has a completed pod whose logs contain at least one of `[PASS]`, `[FAIL]`, `[WARN]`.
questions.hint: Apply a Job with `restartPolicy: Never`, `hostPID: true`, image `aquasec/kube-bench:latest`, args `["run","--targets","node"]`, and hostPath volumes for the three host paths. Then `kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\]'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: kube-bench, namespace: cks-bench }
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  template:
    spec:
      hostPID: true
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: kube-bench
        image: aquasec/kube-bench:latest
        command: ["kube-bench"]
        args: ["run","--targets","node"]
        volumeMounts:
        - { name: var-lib-kubelet, mountPath: /var/lib/kubelet, readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-kubernetes, mountPath: /etc/kubernetes, readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-systemd, mountPath: /etc/systemd, readOnly: true }
      volumes:
      - { name: var-lib-kubelet, hostPath: { path: /var/lib/kubelet } }
      - { name: etc-kubernetes, hostPath: { path: /etc/kubernetes } }
      - { name: etc-systemd, hostPath: { path: /etc/systemd } }
YAML
kubectl -n cks-bench wait --for=condition=complete job/kube-bench --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\]' | head

verification.description: Job kube-bench completed with hostPID and host mounts; logs contain CIS [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WARN]

questions.title: Audit the control plane (--targets master)
questions.teach:
`--targets node` only covers the kubelet/worker checks (CIS section 4). The control-plane checks (apiserver, scheduler, etcd — CIS section 1) live under `--targets master` and only appear when kube-bench runs **on a control-plane node** where those files exist.

**Gotcha:** a master-targets Job landing on a worker finds no control-plane files — pin it to the control-plane node with a nodeSelector + toleration.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-bench`, create a Job named `kube-bench-master` (`aquasec/kube-bench:latest`, args `["run","--targets","master"]`, `hostPID: true`, `restartPolicy: Never`, same three hostPath mounts) that is pinned to the control-plane node so it can read `/etc/kubernetes/manifests`. Wait for completion.

Target: Job `kube-bench-master` completed on the control-plane node; its logs contain a CIS **1.x** master finding (e.g. `[PASS] 1.` or `[FAIL] 1.`).
questions.hint: Add `nodeSelector: { node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: "" }` and a control-plane toleration so it lands on `$CP`. Use args `["run","--targets","master"]`. Then `kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench-master | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\] 1\.'`.

verification.description: Job kube-bench-master ran on the control plane and logged CIS section 1.x (master) findings

questions.title: Remediate a manifest-permission FAIL (scheduler)
questions.teach:
A recurring master `[FAIL]` (CIS 1.1.x) is a static pod manifest under `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` left group/world readable. CIS requires mode `0600` (`rw-------`); fix with `chmod 600 file`. Changing only the mode does NOT restart the pod, so it's safe live. On kind, reach the node with `docker exec $CP`.

**Gotcha:** `stat -c '%a'` drops the leading zero so `0600` prints `600` — leaving it `640` still leaks to the group and FAILs.
questions.prompt:
kube-bench flagged the kube-scheduler manifest on control-plane node `$CP`: setup loosened it to mode `644`. Set `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml` on `$CP` to exactly mode `600`.

Target: `docker exec $CP stat -c '%a' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml` prints `600`.
questions.solution:
docker exec $CP chmod 600 /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml
docker exec $CP stat -c '%a %U:%G' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml   # 600 root:root

questions.title: Protect PKI private-key permissions
questions.teach:
PKI private keys under `/etc/kubernetes/pki/` (CIS 1.1.19/1.1.21) are the crown jewels — anyone who reads `ca.key` can mint certs for any identity. kube-bench requires every `*.key` at mode `0600`. Fix with `chmod 600`; it changes only permission bits, so nothing restarts.

**Gotcha:** certs (`*.crt`) are public and may stay `0644`, but a `*.key` at `640` or `660` still leaks to the group and FAILs — keys must be exactly `600`.
questions.prompt:
kube-bench flagged `/etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.key` on `$CP`: setup loosened it to mode `644`. Set it back to exactly mode `600`.

Target: `docker exec $CP stat -c '%a' /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.key` prints `600`.
questions.solution:
docker exec $CP chmod 600 /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.key
docker exec $CP stat -c '%a %U:%G' /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.key   # 600 root:root

questions.title: Harden the kubelet (read-only port)
questions.teach:
CIS 4.2.x: the kubelet can serve an **unauthenticated read-only port** (`10255`) that leaks pod/node metadata. kube-bench requires it disabled by setting `readOnlyPort: 0` in `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`. Editing the file isn't enough — run `systemctl restart kubelet` for it to take effect.

**Gotcha:** after the restart wait ~15-20s for the node to go `Ready` again; a bad edit can keep the kubelet down and leave the node `NotReady`.
questions.prompt:
On worker `$W1` the kubelet serves its read-only port (seeded as `readOnlyPort: 10255`). Edit `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` on `$W1` so `readOnlyPort: 0`, then restart the kubelet. Give the node ~20s to report `Ready`.

Target: the config on `$W1` has `readOnlyPort: 0` AND node `$W1` is `Ready`.
questions.hint: `docker exec $W1 sed -i 's/^readOnlyPort:.*/readOnlyPort: 0/' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`, then `docker exec $W1 systemctl restart kubelet`.
questions.solution:
docker exec $W1 sed -i 's/^readOnlyPort:.*/readOnlyPort: 0/' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
docker exec $W1 grep readOnlyPort /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml   # readOnlyPort: 0
docker exec $W1 systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl get node $W1   # wait ~20s for Ready

verification.description: node $W1 is still Ready after the kubelet restart

questions.title: Harden the apiserver (NodeRestriction)
questions.teach:
CIS 1.2.x: `NodeRestriction` is a kube-apiserver admission plugin that limits each kubelet to modifying **only its own Node and bound Pods**. Enable it in the `--enable-admission-plugins` flag — a comma-separated list, so append `,NodeRestriction` and keep the others.

**Gotcha:** the kubelet recreates the pod on save (no `kubectl apply`), but a typo takes the apiserver down for ~15-30s — edit carefully and wait.
questions.prompt:
Setup removed `NodeRestriction` from the apiserver's `--enable-admission-plugins`. Edit `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml` on `$CP` so the flag includes `NodeRestriction` again (keep any other plugins), then wait for the apiserver to come back.

Target: the running kube-apiserver has `NodeRestriction` in `--enable-admission-plugins`.
questions.hint: `docker exec $CP ...` edit the manifest: add the line `- --enable-admission-plugins=NodeRestriction` under the kube-apiserver command args (or append `,NodeRestriction` to an existing value). Wait ~20s for the apiserver to restart.
questions.solution:
# Setup removed the flag line, so add it back under the kube-apiserver args:
docker exec $CP sed -i '/^    - kube-apiserver$/a\    - --enable-admission-plugins=NodeRestriction' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
# (If the flag already exists with other plugins, instead append ,NodeRestriction to its value.)
# Wait ~20s for the apiserver to restart, then verify:
kubectl -n kube-system get pod kube-apiserver-$CP -o yaml | grep enable-admission-plugins

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a kube-bench kubelet-config FAIL
questions.teach:
CIS 4.1.9 wants the kubelet config file `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` at mode `0600` or stricter — it holds the kubelet's security settings. kube-bench names the file and expected mode in its `[FAIL]` line; confirm with `stat -c '%a'`.

**Gotcha:** this is a `chmod`-only fix — do NOT restart the kubelet, and don't confuse the file's mode with its `readOnlyPort` content from the previous step.
questions.prompt:
kube-bench reports a `[FAIL]` for the kubelet config file permissions on worker `$W1` — setup loosened `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` to mode `644`. Diagnose which file and mode CIS expects, then fix it. No hint beyond the kube-bench output. Do NOT restart the kubelet.

Target: `docker exec $W1 stat -c '%a' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` prints `600` (and the file still contains `readOnlyPort: 0` from the prior step).
questions.hint: Re-run kube-bench node (or just `docker exec $W1 stat -c '%a' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`) — it's `644`, CIS 4.1.9 wants `600`. `docker exec $W1 chmod 600 /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`.
questions.solution:
# kube-bench 4.1.9: /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml must be 600 or more restrictive.
docker exec $W1 stat -c '%a' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml   # 644 -> too open
docker exec $W1 chmod 600 /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
docker exec $W1 stat -c '%a' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml   # 600

verification.description: kubelet config file on $W1 is exactly mode 600 (diagnose-and-fix)
